sermon.title: Intro to Bible Economics, Part 1
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Opening a present truth series on Bible economics, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that God commands six days of work and a day of rest, and promised supernatural protection to those who kept His feasts. He applies Deuteronomy 15:6 to national debt and to who rules a nation, insists that Christians work, and explains how he keeps the feast days as shadows fulfilled in Christ.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: his figures and statements (national debt of about 18 trillion dollars, the share of communists in China, the percentages of Christians, humanists, Chinese, Latinos and illegal immigrants in America, the history of the five-day workweek, and his claims about the Quran, Muslims, communist nations, politicians and a named presidential candidate’s statements) are his own and are not verified here. One passage at about 13:30 was badly garbled in the captions and is marked [unclear], as are several other words.

chunks.section_question: Should Christians take time to rest? (Mark 6:30-31)
chunks.short_answer: He says “The holidays are just a good time to kick back.” He reads that Jesus told the apostles to come apart into a desert place and rest a while, and says “if Jesus rested and the apostles rested. Shouldn’t we rest,” balancing rest and leisure with productive work.
chunks.text: And why can we do those dumb things because we know how to keep the real thing and we know what the real thing is can I hear an amen. The holidays are just a good time to kick back. Mark 6:30 the apostles told Jesus all they had done and talked he had sent them out and he said to the apostles come apart into a desert place and rest a while if Jesus rested and the apostles rested. Shouldn’t we rest now really we got to balance rest and leisure with work. You got to be productive but we need time to rest their self and we need to work when we work.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then the apostles gathered to Jesus and told Him all things, both what they had done and what they had taught. And He said to them, “Come aside by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a while.” For there were many coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.

faqs.question: What kind of work does he say the Sabbath forbids?
faqs.answer: He says the work is income: “it’s not repairing the screen door it’s not washing the dishes it is making money.”

faqs.question: Did Adam have to work in the garden of Eden?
faqs.answer: He says Adam had to work the garden; God initiated work right at the beginning.

faqs.question: Why did the five-day workweek help businesses?
faqs.answer: He says industries realized overworking people was unprofitable; with five days, eight hours and doubled wages, productivity went off the scale and employees stayed until they retired.

faqs.question: What is the feast of weeks?
faqs.answer: He says the feast of weeks is Pentecost.

faqs.question: Why did God specifically call the men to appear before Him?
faqs.answer: He says God had to get specific with males “because we’re so hard hot headed and so busy golfing and everything on off days.”

faqs.question: Can Christ come any minute?
faqs.answer: He says Christians predict the second coming any minute without thinking about how every jot and tittle of the word must be fulfilled, including these promises not yet restored globally.

faqs.question: What does he say many churches teach instead of Bible truth?
faqs.answer: He says many mega church ministers and pastors teach psychology, prosperity, possibility thinking and positive thinking instead of everyday wholesome living principles.

faqs.question: What does he say about chaplains and the name of Jesus?
faqs.answer: He says chaplains cannot use Jesus in the military and are getting fired, while most Christians just sit back.

faqs.question: Is work part of the Ten Commandments?
faqs.answer: He says work is in the fourth commandment of the Ten Commandments, and a lot of Christians don’t work.

faqs.question: What does he tell people who are not working?
faqs.answer: He says, “stop feeling sorry for yourself get your butt off the chair and work,” clean a pool, clean a motel room, wash cars, do something.

faqs.question: What does he say about Easter and Christmas traditions?
faqs.answer: He says the Easter bunny and Easter eggs have nothing to do with Passover, and Christmas trees and wreaths have nothing to do with His birth; “we know how to keep the real thing.”
